new_statements.quote: The phonology is presented in terms of a Natural Phonology framework, with exceptionless phonetic processes followed in their turn by morphologically conditional rules. As in other Somali varieties (and Cushitic in general), Af Tunni is a tonal accent language, in which tone is determined primarily morphosyntactically. [Publisher blurb.] — First-hand, Tosco 1997 p. 22: "pp 2. SHORT VOWEL CENTRALIZATION. In word-final position short unstressed vowels are neutralized to [ə]"; p. 23: "any short vowel is (under the conditions stated above) assimilated to the nearest H-toned vowel".

new_statements.rule_in_words: Tunni, like Standard Somali, has a tonal accent (pitch accent) system rather than dynamic stress: at most one high tone per word, written with an acute, whose placement is assigned by morphosyntax (gender, number, case; verbal paradigm) rather than by a fixed phonological position. The syllable carrying the H tone is the prominent ('stressed') syllable; unaccented word-final short vowels reduce to [ə]. No default position (initial/penult/final) is stated in any page opened.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in the material opened.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated in the material opened. Sample p. 16 notes that the reduced vowel [ə] 'can occur with H-tone' (agaaranə 'it is green'), i.e. H tone/prominence is not restricted to full vowels.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level tonal accent (Somali-type pitch accent): a high tone ('H') is the only marked tone (abbreviations p. x 'H high tone'; acute accent in transcription, e.g. dobódi 'the jackal', moorόda 'the cattle-pen', qablíl 'tribe'). The sample pages equate H-toned syllables with prominence/'stressed' syllables (p. 22: word-final short unstressed vowels neutralized to [ə]; p. 23: short vowels assimilate to 'the nearest H-toned vowel' in 'a more prominent syllable'). Position of the accent within the word is not stated in any page opened; the blurb says it is determined 'primarily morphosyntactically' (i.e. by gender/number/case and verbal category, cf. TOC §II.1.2 'Tonal patterns and gender', §III.1.5 'Tones on verbs'), not by a phonological default position.
new_statements.identity_note: Af Tunni = Tunni [tqq], Glottolog tunn1238, Digil group of Southern Somali (interriverine area between Brava/Merka and the Juba; informants placed it from Goob Weyn to Eeriile). Tosco 1997 is based on his own 1980s fieldwork with Tunni speakers and notes the dialect is the one most influenced by the Southern Somali koine Maay (maay1238); no sub-dialect is singled out. The publisher blurb and Wikipedia sentence refer to this same variety.
